name: Unending Torment

angles.text: For the Forsaken, the head illustrates the grim humor and unforgiving nature of their queen, Sylvanas Windrunner. It serves as a stark reminder of the Dark Lady's absolute authority and the macabre ingenuity of the Royal Apothecary Society.

Horde adventurers witnessing Faranell's reception of the head gain a direct glimpse into the disturbing practices of their Undercity allies. While effective, the Forsaken methods of endless reanimation and flesh-crafting often unnerve their more honor-bound peers.

faq.answer: The Abominable Head is the severed head of a unique construct that drops when the creature is defeated. Its neck bears the scars of being reattached repeatedly, with each reconnection weakening the flesh and stitches. It serves as proof of a bizarre, recurring punishment inflicted upon the creature, prompting the finder to deliver it to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity for examination.

aliases: why was the head sewn back on
faq.answer: The creature's head was repeatedly stitched back onto its body as a form of torment. According to Master Apothecary Faranell, the creature's state is a cruel and deliberate joke orchestrated by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Each time the construct fell or lost its head, it was pieced back together to continue serving or suffering, resulting in an increasingly fragile neck that eventually gave way once more.
faq.q: Why has the head been reattached so many times?

faq.answer: Master Apothecary Faranell is the head of the Royal Apothecary Society, stationed within the Apothecarium of the Undercity. Under the authority of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner, Faranell oversees the Forsaken apothecaries as they research poisons, plagues, and anatomical alterations. His intimate familiarity with the Dark Lady's projects allows him to immediately identify the origins of the stitched head.

While Faranell does not elaborate on the original identity of the creature, he regards the construct's endless cycle of death and reassembly as a delicious jest by the Dark Lady. Forcing a creature to endure repeated destruction, only to be sloppily reanimated and stitched back together time and time again, embodies Sylvanas's merciless sense of irony and punishment toward her enemies.
faq.q: Why does Sylvanas consider this a cruel joke?

aliases: what will the apothecaries do with it
faq.answer: Upon receiving the battered head, Faranell notes with grim amusement that he has a use for it. As the overseer of the Royal Apothecary Society's grotesque experiments, he regularly repurposes necromantic remnants, flesh, and biological oddities for the development of new concoctions, plagues, and construct reinforcements to aid the Forsaken in their ongoing conflicts.
faq.q: What will Faranell do with the head?

aliases: where to turn in unending torment
faq.answer: The quest is completed by bringing the Abominable Head directly to Master Apothecary Faranell. He resides in the Apothecarium, the alchemical wing located in the southern quadrant of the Undercity. Forsaken adventurers and Horde allies can find him surrounded by bubbling vats, assistants, and test subjects as he oversees the society's research.
faq.q: Where do you turn in the quest Unending Torment?

faq.answer: Because the objective requires delivering the quest item directly to Master Apothecary Faranell inside the Apothecarium of the Undercity, this quest is intended for Horde adventurers. Any Alliance player attempting to approach Faranell would face hostile Undercity guards and death at the hands of the Forsaken upon entering their subterranean stronghold.
faq.q: Can Alliance players turn in this quest?

sections.body: When the towering abomination finally collapses in battle, its head abruptly topples from its shoulders. A close inspection reveals that the neck has not merely been severed once, but stitched, torn away, and reattached numerous times. With each successive reconstruction, the seam has grown more fragile, leaving the head barely clinging to the construct's shoulders. Such shoddy yet persistent patchwork is unusual even for undead constructs, suggesting that this particular abomination was subjected to repeated cycles of destruction and reassembly. Recognizing that ordinary scavengers could not explain such craftsmanship, anyone examining the remains quickly realizes that only the skilled flesh-crafters of the Undercity could identify the origins of this creature.
sections.title: A Loose Stitch

sections.body: Delivering the severed head to the Apothecarium brings it before Master Apothecary Faranell, leader of the Royal Apothecary Society. Far from being surprised by the gruesome specimen, Faranell instantly recognizes the visage. He identifies the repeated reassembly not as an accidental failure of necromancy, but as an intentional and cruel joke devised by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner herself. What specific offense or slight earned the creature such eternal, degrading punishment remains known only to the Dark Lady and her inner circle. Rather than discarding the battered relic, Faranell gleefully accepts the severed head, confident that the Royal Apothecary Society can repurpose it for their ongoing alchemical and necromantic endeavors.
sections.title: The Dark Lady's Jest

summary: Unending Torment begins when a strange abomination is slain, causing its head to topple loose from repeated stitching. Bearing signs of having been severed and reconnected many times over, the relic points toward deliberate dark experimentation within the Forsaken capital. Bringing the grisly prize to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity uncovers the twisted humor behind its repeated reanimation.
